en.headline: Cheuk says 1823 upgrades to take effect in first quarter of 2027
en.dek: The Deputy Chief Secretary said artificial intelligence will analyse repeated complaints so problems can be tackled proactively without waiting for reports.
body: Deputy Chief Secretary for Administration Warner Cheuk Wing-hing said optimisations to the 1823 government hotline service are expected to take effect in the first quarter of 2027.

Speaking at a press conference, Cheuk said the Digital Policy Office will use artificial intelligence to analyse recurring issues, enabling a more proactive approach so that problems can be addressed even before formal complaints are lodged.

In the first seven months of this year 1823 handled more than 1.4 million telephone calls and over 600,000 written submissions. Cheuk acknowledged that while the existing mechanism covers most requests, there remains room to improve handling of cross-department cases, post-complaint monitoring by departments, and trend analysis.
The measures form part of commitments in the latest Policy Address to refine public services and make fuller use of artificial intelligence in government administration.

zh.headline: 卓永興：1823優化措施明年首季落實
zh.dek: 政務司副司長表示將以人工智能分析重覆問題，冀做到無需投訴亦可主動處理。
body: 政務司副司長卓永興表示，1823服務的優化措施預計於明年首季落實。
他在記者會上指出，數字辦會使用人工智能分析重覆性問題，採取主動防禦方式，做到不需要投訴都能主動處理問題。
今年首7個月，1823共接獲逾140萬個電話及60多萬個書面訴求。卓永興承認現時機制基本上能處理所有訴求，但在跨部門個案處理效率、部門投訴後監察及個案趨勢分析等方面仍有提升空間。
有關措施屬最新施政報告承諾，旨在優化公共服務及善用人工智能改革公共管理。
